## Summary
- Replace `cloudposse/github-action-secret-outputs@main` with a local composite action, `.github/actions/secret-output`, in all four jobs of `nova-run-examples.yaml`.

## Why
The cloudposse action is a Docker action. Its image is built during job set-up `FROM public.ecr.aws/docker/library/alpine:3.19.1`, and since 2026-10-14 that pull fails with `429 Too Many Requests – Data limit exceeded` on GitHub's shared runners. `setup-instance` fails, and with it every integration and example job, on every branch including main (e.g. #516, #544 and the Dependabot PRs). The workflow can't pre-pull or redirect the image, because it's built before any step runs.

## Benefits
- Integration and example jobs run again on all PRs and on main.
- No image pull at all, so no exposure to registry rate limits.
- `GPG_PASSWORD` and the instance access token no longer pass through a third-party action pinned to `@main`.

## How
The composite action runs the same `gpg` symmetric encrypt/decrypt on the runner (`gpg` ships with `ubuntu-latest`). It keeps the inputs (`op`, `in`, `secret`), the output (`out`), the `::add-mask::` on decode, and the ciphertext format. Inputs go in via `env`, not inline expressions. `--pinentry-mode loopback` is added so `--passphrase` works on any GnuPG 2.x.

## Test plan
- [x] Ran the action's exact `run:` script in Docker: the round trip works on GnuPG 2.2.27 (`ubuntu:22.04`) and 2.4.9 (`alpine`), with a passphrase containing quotes and `$`. An unknown `op` is rejected.
- [x] Compatible with the cloudposse script in both directions (theirs encodes → ours decodes, and the reverse).
- [x] Both YAML files parse.
- [ ] This PR's own `nova-run-examples` run: `setup-instance` encodes, and the decode steps in `create_motion_group_models`, `test-integration` and `cleanup-instance` succeed.

## Notes for reviewers
- `uv-audit` has a separate failure (Python 3.15 picked, no pyarrow wheels), fixed in its own PR.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
GH_PAGER=cat gh pr create --base main --head ci/secret-output-composite --title "ci: replace the Docker secret-outputs action with a local gpg composite action" --body-file $B; rm -f $B

## Summary
- Pin the `uv-audit` job to Python 3.12 via `UV_PYTHON`, as every other workflow already does.

## Why
`requires-python` is `>=3.12` and `.python-version` is gitignored, so `uv python install` now resolves to CPython **3.15.0**. pyarrow 25.0.0 has no 3.15 wheels; uv falls back to the sdist, the CMake build fails, and the job errors out before the audit runs. This happens on every branch, main included (weekly run 2026-10-19, push 2026-10-21).

## Benefits
- The audit actually runs again, so dependency advisories are reported instead of hidden behind a build error.
- Audits the Python version the SDK is developed and tested on.

## Test plan
- [x] Locally with `UV_PYTHON=3.12`: `uv python install`, `uv sync --extra nova-rerun-bridge --extra wandelscript --extra novax`, then `uv audit --preview-features audit-command`. Everything installs from wheels and the audit runs.
- [ ] This PR's own `uv-audit` run.

## Notes for reviewers
The job is **expected to stay red after this lands**, for a real reason: the audit reports 40 known vulnerabilities in aiohttp 3.14.3, certifi 2026.7.22, multidict 6.7.1 and pillow 12.3.0. Those are the packages Dependabot PRs #540–#543 bump. Their CI is red only because of this issue and the secret-outputs pull (#545), so merging both unblocks them.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
GH_PAGER=cat gh pr create --base main --head ci/uv-audit-python-312 --title "ci(uv-audit): pin Python 3.12 so dependencies install from wheels" --body-file $B; rm -f $B

input.command:
B=$(mktemp) && cat > $B <<'EOF'
## Summary
- Pin the `uv-audit` job to Python 3.12 via `UV_PYTHON`, as every other workflow already does.
- Bump four dependencies with open advisories: aiohttp 3.14.3 → 3.14.4, certifi 2026.7.22 → 2026.10.19, multidict 6.7.1 → 6.9.1 (yarl 1.24.5 → 1.25.1 follows), pillow 12.3.0 → 13.0.0.
- Raise the core requirement floor to `pillow>=13.0.0`.

## Why
`uv-audit` has been red on every branch, main included, without auditing anything. `requires-python` is `>=3.12` and `.python-version` is gitignored, so `uv python install` now picks the newest CPython (3.15.x). pyarrow and scipy have no wheels for it, uv falls back to source builds, and those fail before the audit runs. On 3.12 the audit runs and reports **40 known vulnerabilities** in aiohttp (8), certifi (2), multidict (2) and pillow (28).

## Benefits
- `uv-audit` is green again and reports real advisories, instead of hiding them behind a build error.
- SDK users get fixes for 40 published advisories, including Pillow's Ghostscript argument injection (GHSA-w889-685w-c8fh) and certifi's compromised emSign root CAs.
- `pillow>=13.0.0` keeps a vulnerable Pillow from satisfying the requirement, matching the `urllib3>=2.8.0` floor from #534.

## How
The versions are the same as Dependabot #540–#543. The exception is the pillow floor: #542 *lowered* it from `>=12.3.0` to `>=10.0.0`, which this PR doesn't do. Only these five packages move in `uv.lock`. The `novapolicy` extra still declares `Pillow>=10.0.0`, but the core requirement wins whenever the SDK is installed.

## Test plan
- [x] `UV_PYTHON=3.12`: `uv sync --extra nova-rerun-bridge --extra wandelscript --extra novax`, then `uv audit --preview-features audit-command` reports "Found no known vulnerabilities … in 118 packages" (exit 0).
- [x] `PYTHONPATH=. uv run pytest -m "not integration"` with all extras: 1059 passed, 6 skipped. Covers Pillow 13, a major version.
- [x] `uv run ty check`: all checks passed.
- [ ] This PR's own CI run.

## Notes for reviewers
- Dependabot should close #540–#543 by itself once main has these versions.
- #545 (secret-outputs) is independent. Its `uv-audit` goes green once this is on main.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

content.text:
Yes for the four that #546 covered. For the other two open Dependabot PRs, no:

| PR | State | Status |
|---|---|---|
| #540 aiohttp → 3.14.4 | closed by Dependabot | done |
| #542 pillow → 13.0.0 | closed by Dependabot | done |
| #541 multidict → 6.9.1 | still open | **obsolete**: main already has 6.9.1. Dependabot should close it on its next check. |
| #543 certifi → 2026.10.19 | still open | **obsolete**, for the same reason |
| #536 group, 16 updates | open | **still relevant**: none of the four packages is in it. It updates the API client to 26.7.3, pydantic, scipy, numpy, nats-py, `python-statemachine`, `ty` 0.0.69 → 0.0.89 and others. |
| #518 `examples/your-nova-app` lock | open, last updated 09-21 | **still relevant, but outdated**: it only touches the example app's lock file, and bumps aiohttp only to 3.14.3, which still has the 8 advisories. The example needs aiohttp 3.14.4 too. |

Two caveats on #536:

Neither #516 nor #544 has a usable integration result yet, and neither failure points at the PRs' own code. I've started re-runs and am watching them.

- **#516:** the run failed in `setup-instance` before any SDK code ran. When the setup script connected to the newly created NOVA instance, the instance was still serving a self-signed certificate. That's most likely a timing problem in instance setup. The certifi bump from #546 is an unlikely cause, because #546's own integration run passed with the same version.
- **#544:** its run never started. Dependabot's #536 run took the waiting slot and cancelled it.
- **#536:** my re-run of #516 cancelled Dependabot's run in turn. Runs from other PRs can take the slot too, which I hadn't accounted for.
- **Other checks:** typecheck/lint, `uv-audit`, CodeQL, dependency review and yamllint pass on both PRs.

The re-runs go one at a time, in this order: #516, then #544, then #536. Each starts only after the previous one is running. If #516 fails on the same certificate error again, it's a recurring problem in `scripts/create_nova_instance.py`, and that script should wait until the instance serves its real certificate before connecting.

I haven't closed #541 or #543. Dependabot should close them by itself, or I can close them with a comment pointing to #546.

feat(rerun): wall-clock timeline option for multi-robot programs

The bridge places each motion group's trajectories back to back on the
shared time_interval timeline: a trajectory starts where the group's
previous one ended, and time spent waiting (for a lock, a signal, another
robot) is dropped. Two robots that took turns in reality therefore replay
as moving simultaneously — the interlock example looked like a collision
on every cycle although the log showed strict alternation.

Add `wall_clock=True` to NovaRerunBridge and nova.viewers.Rerun: each
trajectory then starts at the real elapsed time since the bridge was
created, so waits show up as the robot standing still and the replay
follows what happened. Default behaviour is unchanged. Unit tests cover
both placements; the interlock example enables the option.

## Summary
- Add `wall_clock: bool = False` to `nova.viewers.Rerun` and `NovaRerunBridge`. When enabled, each trajectory is placed on the rerun timeline at the real time elapsed since the bridge was created, not directly after the motion group's previous trajectory.
- Add `NovaRerunBridge.elapsed_seconds()`, which returns the wall-clock timeline's origin offset.

## Why
The bridge packs each motion group's trajectories back to back: a trajectory starts where the group's previous one ended, so any time a robot spent waiting (for a lock, an IO signal, another robot) disappears from the replay. In multi-robot programs, two robots that took turns in reality replay as moving at the same time. The two-robot interlock example (#544) looked like a collision on every cycle, although the logs showed strict alternation.

## Benefits
- Replays of coordinated multi-robot programs show what actually happened, with waits visible as a robot standing still. That makes interlock or signal problems diagnosable from the viewer.
- Opt-in: the default timeline is unchanged for existing programs.

## How
Wall-clock mode reads `time.monotonic()` against an origin taken when the bridge is created. The default path still uses the per-motion-group timers.

## Test plan
- [x] `PYTHONPATH=. uv run pytest tests/nova_rerun_bridge/test_nova_rerun_bridge.py tests/test_viewers.py`: 69 passed. The new tests cover both placements.
- [x] `PYTHONPATH=. uv run pytest -m "not integration"` on Python 3.12 with all extras: 1105 passed, 6 skipped.
- [x] `uv run ruff format --check .`, `uv run ruff check .`, `uv run ty check`

## Notes for reviewers
- The interlock example in #544 is the first user. Whichever of the two merges second switches that example to `viewer=nova.viewers.Rerun(wall_clock=True)`, a one-line change.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF

I opened PR 1 as #547: the rerun `wall_clock` option, built on current main with the code exactly as on the lab branch. It's pushed, and CI hasn't run on it yet.

**What's in it:** a `wall_clock=False` option on `nova.viewers.Rerun` and `NovaRerunBridge`, plus tests for both timeline modes. The two-robot example's switch to `wall_clock=True` isn't included, because the example only exists in #544. Whichever of #544 and #547 merges second adds that one line; the PR's reviewer notes say so.

**Checks:**
- **Locally on Python 3.12:** 1,105 unit tests passed, the 69 rerun and viewer tests passed, and ruff and ty are clean.
- **CI:** its integration run is queued behind a release-please run that's in progress. Nothing was waiting in the queue, so my push didn't cancel anyone else's run.

**Correction to my earlier explanation of the "54 failures":** they come from **Python 3.14**, not from a broken worktree setup. `.python-version` is gitignored, so a fresh worktree's venv gets the newest Python uv has installed, the same cause as the `uv-audit` break. On 3.12 the suite is fully green. I've updated my notes to always pin 3.12 in new worktrees.

content.text: <total_tokens>14995397 tokens left</total_tokens>

Torsten's branch adds **external TCP support** to planning and execution. It's built on top of `lab/pause-auto-resume`, so it contains all our lab work as well. His own changes are five commits across 8 files (+105/−37), from 2026-10-14 to 10-23, and there's no PR yet.

**What his commits change:**
- **External TCP:**
  - **Where:** a new optional `external_tcp` / `external_tcp_name` parameter, passed through `MotionGroup` planning, motion loading and execution, `RobotCell`, simulation and `motion_group_setup`.
  - **Effect:** when it's set, the setup's `external_tool_offset` comes from the controller's TCP list. Motion is then planned relative to the moving coordinate system of the robot's kinematic chain, with the tool fixed.
- **API client pin:** changed to `wandelbots_api_client==26.9.0+a3190.82740d37.508444`. That's another per-MR build from the internal GitLab registry (service-manager !3190, which presumably adds the external-tool fields), replacing the lab's !3081 build.
- **State machine ("Fiddle with state machine"):**
  - **Change:** `TrajectoryExecutionMachine.process_motion_state()` takes an optional `motion_id`, and the cursor passes its own. Trajectory frames whose `details.trajectory` doesn't match the cursor's motion are then no longer treated as frames of this execution.

**Points to raise with Torsten:**
1. **State machine:** this changes #516's code, now on main. The `armed` state already filters stale end-state frames from the previous trajectory. Matching on the trajectory ID is a stricter, ID-based version of the same idea, and may be better. But it changes which frames reach the armed/transient/rest logic, and it isn't covered by tests in his commit. It should go to main as its own PR with tests, not mixed into the external-TCP work.
2. **Branch base:** a PR from this branch to main would include all 25 lab commits, including the ones now split across #544, #547 and the upcoming pause-on-IO PRs. The branch would need rebuilding on main, keeping only his five commits. Those touch `motion_group.py`, which the pause-on-IO and standstill PRs change too, so the merge order between his work and PRs 4 and 5 matters.
3. **Internal client pin:** like PR 6's `auto_resume`, his work can only land on main once a public client with the external-tool fields is released.

Want me to check which public client versions, if any, already have the external-tool fields, or how his five commits would apply to current main?

                tcp=tcp,

I dry-ran Torsten's commits two ways. Mechanically both go through, but his commits break 46 unit tests on his own branch, and his execution change needs a client field that #538's version doesn't have.

**1. His commits on current main**
- **Applying:** all four code commits apply cleanly. Only the client pin conflicts in `pyproject.toml`/`uv.lock`, and I kept main's side.
- **Client:** I tested with #538's public `26.9.0.dev23`, and also checked every public build up to `dev33`. They all have `external_tool_offset`, which planning needs. None has `AddTrajectoryRequest.external_tcp`, which his execution commit `8977e9b5` sends. With those builds Pydantic silently drops the field (`ty` warns about exactly that), so execution would ignore the external TCP. For now, only his internal `26.9.0+a3190` build carries it.
- **Tests:** main with only the `dev23` pin is green (1,103 passed). With his commits on top, 41 tests fail.
- **His own branch:** it fails the same way, with 46 failures, while the lab tip underneath is green (814 passed). So the breakage comes from his commits, not from moving them to main:

| His commit | Effect on the tests |
|---|---|
| `ff7a5711` add external tool offset (= #538's code) | all pass |
| `8977e9b5` add external TCP to execution | 34 collection errors |
| `db50c477` reorder arguments | 32 failures. `ty` also flags `SimulatedRobot._plan` as an invalid override of `AbstractRobot._plan`. |
| `02a92ee2` fiddle with state machine | 9 more. Executor tests time out and a cursor test completes late, which fits the trajectory-ID filter dropping frames that tests (and maybe controllers) send under a different ID. |

The wandelscript tests (32 of the failures) hit a `NotImplementedError` from the parser hook. I haven't traced that further.

**2. His branch combined with main's additions (datasets etc.), like `lab/pause-auto-resume-main`**
- **Merging into `lab/pause-auto-resume-main`:** clean, no conflicts. The pin resolves to his internal `a3190` build, still served from the internal GitLab registry.
- **Missing #516:** `lab/pause-auto-resume-main` stops at main's #546, so it doesn't have #516's squash merge yet. Merging current main into it conflicts in the 12 state-machine files. The squash is identical to #516's rebased head, which the lab already contains, so resolving to the lab's side is correct.

1. **Tests:** fix the 46 failing tests on his branch, starting with the argument reorder and the `_plan` override.
2. **Execution field:** a public client release that includes `AddTrajectoryRequest.external_tcp` (service-manager !3190) before the execution part can go to main. #538, planning only, works with `dev23` today.
3. **State-machine filter:** this goes as its own small PR against main with tests, since it changes #516's frame handling.

I prepared `lab/pause-auto-resume-main` locally in your main checkout; it isn't pushed. It now has current main (including #516) and Torsten's external-TCP branch, but his commits bring 46 unit-test failures with them.

**The two merges:**
1. **`8f2e1033`, main into the lab branch:** 12 conflicts in the state machine, cursor and their tests. Main's #516 is byte-identical to the lab's `cba1c40b` on all 12 files, so every conflict comes from the pause and standstill work built on top. I resolved them all to the lab's side, and the branch's content is unchanged.
2. **`7aaed37b`, Torsten's branch:** merged with no conflicts. The client pin follows his branch to `26.9.0+a3190`, still from the internal GitLab registry. `uv lock --check` confirms the lock is consistent.

**Results on Python 3.12, all extras:**
- **Tests:** 1,187 passed, **46 failed**. They're the same 46, in the same files, as on his own branch. The lab code underneath was green before his merge (1,233 passed per your notes), so the failures come from his commits. The extra passes compared with his branch are main's datasets tests.
- **ruff:** clean.
- **ty:** 4 errors.
  - 3 are in `tests/interlock/test_interlock.py`. The lab's copy doesn't have the `ty: ignore` marks I added in #544.
  - The 4th was cut off by my output filter, and I didn't re-run it. It's most likely `SimulatedRobot._plan`'s invalid override from his argument reorder, which `ty` already flagged in the main-based dry run.

The branch is 6 commits ahead of `origin/lab/pause-auto-resume-main`. Should I push it? If Torsten builds from it, he'll see the failing tests too, which may be useful for him.

Two bugs in Torsten's commits explain 46 of the 46 failures. With both fixed, all 660 tests in those suites pass.

## 1. Renamed parameter not updated in the simulator: 32 tests
**Error:** `TypeError: SimulatedRobot._plan() got an unexpected keyword argument 'external_tcp'`
- **Cause:** his later commits rename the parameter of `AbstractRobot._plan` to `external_tcp`. `SimulatedRobot._plan` (`nova/cell/simulation.py:153`) still has the old name, `external_tool_offset_name`. Every planning call against the simulated cell fails.
- **Affected:** all 30 wandelscript failures (examples, move, motion, programs, runtime, run-twice, metamodel doctests). The 2 `test_runner` assertion failures are the same thing: the program dies on that error, so the runner never reaches the expected state.
- **Also `ty`:** this is `ty`'s "invalid override of `_plan`" error.
- **Fix:** rename the parameter in `SimulatedRobot._plan` to `external_tcp`. That one-line change makes all 32 pass.

## 2. Trajectory-ID filter drops every test frame: 14 tests
**Error:** 13× `TimeoutError`, plus 1× "Monitor returned after 5 states — expected completion … (frame 3)"
- **Cause:** "Fiddle with state machine" (`02a92ee2`) makes `process_motion_state()` ignore trajectory frames whose `details.trajectory` differs from the cursor's `motion_id`. The test fakes use inconsistent IDs: frames say `trajectory="traj-1"` while the cursor gets `motion_id="test-motion"`. So every frame is discarded, and the executions never see motion start or end.
- **Affected:**
  - 4 in `test_move_forward_adapter` (IO-pause resume, signal loss)
  - 7 in `test_trajectory_executor_session` (synchronized execution, monitors, IO overlay)
  - 2 in `test_pause_auto_resume` (synchronized auto-resume)
  - 1 in `test_process_motion_group_state` (end then standstill)
- **Proof:** reverting only the filter makes all 14 pass.
- **For Torsten:** on a real controller the IDs probably match, since `motion_id` comes from `add_trajectory`, so the filter may well be correct. If it stays, the tests' fakes need matching IDs, plus a test that frames from a *different* trajectory are ignored. It also overlaps with #516's stale end-state filter in the `armed` state, so it deserves its own small PR against main.

## Remaining `ty` errors (not test failures)
3 errors in `tests/interlock/test_interlock.py`. The lab copy doesn't have the `ty: ignore` marks I added in #544, so they disappear once the lab picks those up.

Both experiments were temporary, and the worktree is reset. `lab/pause-auto-resume-main` still contains his commits unchanged (local only, not pushed).

---
name: "@wandelbots/wandelbots-nova: Build dev wheel"
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
jobs:
  build-wheel:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with: {fetch-depth: 0}
      - name: Gather metadata
        id: meta
        run: |
          BRANCH="${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"                 # e.g. feat/new-ui
          SAFE_BRANCH=$(echo "$BRANCH" | tr '/' '-')  # feat-new-ui
          echo "branch=$SAFE_BRANCH"   >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - name: Build wheel
        run: |
          COMMIT=$(git rev-parse --short=12 HEAD)     # 1a2b3c4d5e6f
          DATE=$(date +%Y%m%d)                        # 20250606
          BASE_VER=$(grep -m1 '^version' pyproject.toml | cut -d'"' -f2)  # 1.12.0
          python -m pip install --upgrade build
          python -m build --wheel --outdir dist
          WHEEL_ORIG=$(ls dist/*.whl)
          NAME="wandelbots_nova-${BASE_VER}.dev${DATE}+${{ steps.meta.outputs.branch }}.${COMMIT}.whl"
          echo "Renaming wheel to: $NAME"
          mv "$WHEEL_ORIG" "dist/$NAME"
      - name: Upload wheel artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v6
        with:
          name: wheel-${{ steps.meta.outputs.branch }}
          path: dist/*.whl
          retention-days: 7
      - name: Install instructions
        run: |
          echo ""
          echo "------------------------------------------------------------"
          echo "📦  Install this build straight from GitHub:"
          echo ""
          echo "    pip install \"wandelbots-nova @ git+https://github.com/wandelbotsgmbh/wandelbots-nova.git@${{ github.sha }}\""
          echo ""
          echo "(The command pins to the commit that produced this workflow run.)"
          echo "------------------------------------------------------------"

    api_client,
    states: asyncio.Queue | None = None,
    controller: str = "controller-a",
    trajectory_id: str = "traj-1",
    cell: str = "cell",
) -> MagicMock:
    """A motion group as the executor sees it: an address, a loader and a stream."""
    queue = states if states is not None else asyncio.Queue()

    async def stream():
        # A real motion-group stream is always live; an idle state satisfies the
        # cursor's startup handshake before any trajectory progress arrives.
        yield state(True)
        while True:
            yield await queue.get()

    group._controller_id = controller
    group._api_client = api_client
    group._load_planned_motion = AsyncMock(return_value=trajectory_id)
    group.stream_state = stream
    return group

"""
Example: a motion-enable signal per robot — the robot moves only while its IO reads True.
``execute()`` / ``plan_and_execute()`` accept ``pause_on_io``: an IO condition the robot
controller watches while it runs the trajectory. While the condition holds, the controller
pauses the robot gracefully on path; the SDK keeps the execution open, waits for the
condition to clear and resumes, so the ``await`` returns only when the trajectory is
traversed (see docs/architecture/adr/002-io-pause-is-resumable.md).
``motion_enable_signal(io)`` builds the fail-safe form of that condition: the robot is
allowed to move while the signal reads True and pauses as soon as it reads False. A PLC
drops the signal to stop the robot — and a broken wire or a lost Profinet connection reads
False as well, so the robot stops in that case too. Resume is automatic once the signal is
back.
The signal is per motion group: give every robot its own signal to stop them individually,
or the same signal to several robots to stop them together. Both controller IOs
(``IOOrigin.CONTROLLER``) and bus IOs such as Profinet variables (``IOOrigin.BUS_IO``) work.
This example runs two virtual robots (KUKA + UR), each enabled by its own controller
output, and drives the signals from a second task while they move: first only the KUKA
loses its enable, then both, then both get it back and finish.
Who resumes the pause is selectable (ADR 002 addendum): by default the SDK sends the resume
start once the signal is back; ``--resume=controller`` (or ``NOVA_PAUSE_RESUME=controller``)
lets the robot controller resume by itself (``PauseOnIO.auto_resume``, needs a controller and
API client built with robotics/wbr!2384).
Prerequisites:
- A NOVA instance (see .env / NOVA_API, NOVA_ACCESS_TOKEN)
- Run this example script:
    PYTHONPATH=. uv run python examples/pause_on_signal.py
"""
import asyncio
from math import pi
import nova

57:    await asyncio.sleep(3.0)

"""Smoke probe for external-TCP planning and execution on a virtual UR10e.

Checks the plumbing only, not the geometry:
  1. plan with tcp only (baseline) and with an external TCP (external_tool_offset)
  2. compare the two joint trajectories
  3. execute the external-TCP plan (add_trajectory carries external_tcp)
The probe controller is removed at the end.
"""

import asyncio
import time

from nova import Nova, api
from nova.actions import linear
from nova.cell.controllers import virtual_controller
from nova.types import Pose

CONTROLLER = "ext-tcp-probe"
EXT_TCP = "ext"


def log(msg: str) -> None:
    print(f"[probe {time.strftime('%H:%M:%S')}] {msg}", flush=True)


async def main() -> None:
    async with Nova() as nova:
        cell = nova.cell()
        controller = await cell.ensure_controller(
            virtual_controller(
                name=CONTROLLER,
                manufacturer=api.models.Manufacturer.UNIVERSALROBOTS,
                type="universalrobots-ur10e",
            )
        )
        try:
            mg = controller[0]
            api_client = nova._api_client
            await api_client.virtual_controller_api.add_virtual_controller_tcp(
                cell=cell.cell_id,
                controller=CONTROLLER,
                motion_group=mg.id,
                tcp=EXT_TCP,
                robot_tcp_data=api.models.RobotTcpData(
                    name=EXT_TCP,
                    position=api.models.Vector3d([0.0, 0.0, 200.0]),
                    orientation=api.models.RotationVector([0.0, 0.0, 0.0]),
                ),
            )
            tcps = await mg.tcp_names()
            log(f"tcps on {mg.id}: {tcps}")
            tcp = next(t for t in tcps if t != EXT_TCP)

            start = await mg.tcp_pose(tcp)
            target = start @ Pose((0, 0, 50, 0, 0, 0))
            actions = [linear(target)]
            log(f"tcp={tcp} start={start} target={target}")

            base = await mg.plan(actions, tcp=tcp)
            log(f"plan without external tcp: {len(base.joint_positions)} samples")

            try:
                ext = await mg.plan(actions, tcp=tcp, external_tcp=EXT_TCP)
            except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
                log(f"PLAN with external_tcp FAILED: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
                return
            log(f"plan with external tcp: {len(ext.joint_positions)} samples")
            diff = max(
                abs(a - b)
                for pa, pb in zip(base.joint_positions[-1].root, ext.joint_positions[-1].root)
                for a, b in [(pa, pb)]
            )
            log(f"final joints differ by up to {diff:.4f} rad -> external offset applied: {diff > 1e-6}")

            try:
                await mg.execute(ext, tcp, actions, external_tcp=EXT_TCP)
                log("EXECUTE with external_tcp: completed")
            except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
                log(f"EXECUTE with external_tcp FAILED: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
        finally:
            await cell.delete_robot_controller(CONTROLLER)
            log(f"removed {CONTROLLER}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

"""Smoke probe for external-TCP planning and execution on a virtual UR10e.

Checks the plumbing only, not the geometry:
  1. plan with tcp only (baseline) and with an external TCP (external_tool_offset)
  2. compare the two joint trajectories
  3. execute the external-TCP plan (add_trajectory carries external_tcp)
The probe controller is removed at the end.
"""

import asyncio
import time

from nova import Nova, api
from nova.actions import linear
from nova.cell.controllers import virtual_controller
from nova.types import Pose

CONTROLLER = "ext-tcp-probe"
EXT_TCP = "ext"


def log(msg: str) -> None:
    print(f"[probe {time.strftime('%H:%M:%S')}] {msg}", flush=True)


async def main() -> None:
    async with Nova() as nova:
        cell = nova.cell()
        controller = await cell.ensure_controller(
            virtual_controller(
                name=CONTROLLER,
                manufacturer=api.models.Manufacturer.UNIVERSALROBOTS,
                type="universalrobots-ur10e",
            )
        )
        try:
            mg = controller[0]
            api_client = nova.api
            await api_client.virtual_controller_api.add_virtual_controller_tcp(
                cell=cell.cell_id,
                controller=CONTROLLER,
                motion_group=mg.id,
                tcp=EXT_TCP,
                robot_tcp_data=api.models.RobotTcpData(
                    name=EXT_TCP,
                    position=[0.0, 0.0, 200.0],
                    orientation=[0.0, 0.0, 0.0],
                ),
            )
            tcps = await mg.tcp_names()
            log(f"tcps on {mg.id}: {tcps}")
            tcp = next(t for t in tcps if t != EXT_TCP)

            start = await mg.tcp_pose(tcp)
            target = start @ Pose((0, 0, 50, 0, 0, 0))
            actions = [linear(target)]
            log(f"tcp={tcp} start={start} target={target}")

            base = await mg.plan(actions, tcp=tcp)
            log(f"plan without external tcp: {len(base.joint_positions)} samples")

            try:
                ext = await mg.plan(actions, tcp=tcp, external_tcp=EXT_TCP)
            except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
                log(f"PLAN with external_tcp FAILED: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
                return
            log(f"plan with external tcp: {len(ext.joint_positions)} samples")
            diff = max(
                abs(a - b)
                for pa, pb in zip(base.joint_positions[-1], ext.joint_positions[-1])
                for a, b in [(pa, pb)]
            )
            log(f"final joints differ by up to {diff:.4f} rad -> external offset applied: {diff > 1e-6}")

            try:
                await mg.execute(ext, tcp, actions, external_tcp=EXT_TCP)
                log("EXECUTE with external_tcp: completed")
            except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
                log(f"EXECUTE with external_tcp FAILED: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
        finally:
            await cell.delete_robot_controller(CONTROLLER)
            log(f"removed {CONTROLLER}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

"""Smoke probe for external-TCP planning and execution on a virtual UR10e.

Checks the plumbing only, not the geometry:
  1. plan with tcp only (baseline) and with an external TCP (external_tool_offset)
  2. compare the two joint trajectories
  3. execute the external-TCP plan (add_trajectory carries external_tcp)
The probe controller is removed at the end.
"""

import asyncio
import time

from nova import Nova, api
from nova.actions import linear
from nova.cell.controllers import virtual_controller
from nova.types import Pose

CONTROLLER = "ext-tcp-probe"
EXT_TCP = "ext"


def log(msg: str) -> None:
    print(f"[probe {time.strftime('%H:%M:%S')}] {msg}", flush=True)


async def main() -> None:
    async with Nova() as nova:
        cell = nova.cell()
        controller = await cell.ensure_controller(
            virtual_controller(
                name=CONTROLLER,
                manufacturer=api.models.Manufacturer.UNIVERSALROBOTS,
                type="universalrobots-ur10e",
            )
        )
        try:
            mg = controller[0]
            api_client = nova.api
            await api_client.virtual_controller_api.add_virtual_controller_tcp(
                cell=cell.cell_id,
                controller=CONTROLLER,
                motion_group=mg.id,
                tcp=EXT_TCP,
                robot_tcp_data=api.models.RobotTcpData(
                    name=EXT_TCP,
                    position=[0.0, 0.0, 200.0],
                    orientation=[0.0, 0.0, 0.0],
                ),
            )
            for attempt in range(30):
                listed = await api_client.virtual_controller_api.list_virtual_controller_tcps(
                    cell=cell.cell_id, controller=CONTROLLER, motion_group=mg.id
                )
                names = [t.id for t in listed] if isinstance(listed, list) else str(listed)
                if isinstance(names, list) and EXT_TCP in names:
                    break
                await asyncio.sleep(1)
            log(f"virtual controller reports tcps {names} after {attempt + 1} polls")
            mg = (await cell.controller(CONTROLLER))[0]  # fresh object, no cached description
            tcps = await mg.tcp_names()
            log(f"tcps on {mg.id}: {tcps}")
            tcp = next(t for t in tcps if t != EXT_TCP)

            start = await mg.tcp_pose(tcp)
            target = start @ Pose((0, 0, 50, 0, 0, 0))
            actions = [linear(target)]
            log(f"tcp={tcp} start={start} target={target}")

            base = await mg.plan(actions, tcp=tcp)
            log(f"plan without external tcp: {len(base.joint_positions)} samples")

            try:
                ext = await mg.plan(actions, tcp=tcp, external_tcp=EXT_TCP)
            except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
                log(f"PLAN with external_tcp FAILED: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
                return
            log(f"plan with external tcp: {len(ext.joint_positions)} samples")
            diff = max(
                abs(a - b)
                for pa, pb in zip(base.joint_positions[-1], ext.joint_positions[-1])
                for a, b in [(pa, pb)]
            )
            log(f"final joints differ by up to {diff:.4f} rad -> external offset applied: {diff > 1e-6}")

            try:
                await mg.execute(ext, tcp, actions, external_tcp=EXT_TCP)
                log("EXECUTE with external_tcp: completed")
            except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
                log(f"EXECUTE with external_tcp FAILED: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
        finally:
            await cell.delete_robot_controller(CONTROLLER)
            log(f"removed {CONTROLLER}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

**Live results so far, on branch tip `8679ff88` against NOVA 26.9.0-33:**

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| `pause_on_signal`, SDK resume | ✅ The KUKA paused on its signal, then the UR too. Both resumed when the signals came back, and both finished. |
| `pause_on_signal`, controller resume (`auto_resume`) | ✅ On fresh controllers: start requests carried `auto_resume=True`, the controller reported `WaitForIO` at a standstill while the signal was off, resumed by itself, and both robots finished. |
| External TCP, planning | ✅ The server accepts `external_tool_offset` and applies it: the same move plans to final joints up to 2.6 rad apart. Some moves hit singularities under the external-TCP interpretation, which is a geometry question rather than a bug. |
| External TCP, execution (`add_trajectory` with `external_tcp`) | ⚠️ **Not verified.** The run was cut off by the network loss. |
| Interlock two-robot example | not run yet |

**Findings along the way:**
- **Example rerun:** `pause_on_signal` can fail when re-run against the controllers it leaves running, because it plans from the previous end pose and hits a joint limit. It also exits with code 0 even when the program fails.
- **Instance bug:** on this NOVA build, adding a TCP to a virtual controller breaks the motion-group description endpoint ("not part of controller") indefinitely, so the probe used `Flange` as the external TCP.
- **Possible leftover:** the probe's cleanup ran after the network was gone, so a virtual controller `ext-tcp-probe` may still be on the instance. I'll remove it once I can reach it.

Once you're connected again, tell me and I'll do the cleanup, re-run the external-TCP execution and run the interlock example.

**Verification:** nit. import logging
import random
import uuid
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator, Iterable, Sequence

import nats
from nats.js.api import KeyValueConfig
from nats.js.client import KeyValue
from nats.js.errors import (
    BadRequestError,
    KeyNotFoundError,
    KeyWrongLastSequenceError,
    NotFoundError,
)
from nats.js.kv import KV_DEL, KV_PURGE
from pydantic import ValidationError

from nova.interlock.models import (
    BUCKET_TEMPLATE,
    AlreadyHeldError,
    ForeignRelease,
    Grant,
    InterlockTimeout,
    LockId,
    LockRecord,
)

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

_MAX_VALUE_SIZE = 4 * 1024
_MAX_BUCKET_BYTES = _MAX_VALUE_SIZE * 512

#: Upper bound on a single watch-based wait.  A missed wake-up costs at most
#: this before the acquire loop re-attempts; a delete wakes waiters immediately.
_WATCH_WAIT_CAP = 5.0

#: Placeholder holder id for KV entries whose payload does not parse.  Such an
#: entry blocks acquisition (treated as held) and is surfaced by
#: :meth:`InterlockClient.inspect` so an operator can ``force_release`` it.
CORRUPT_HOLDER = "<unparseable>"


class InterlockClient:
    """Per-robot client for the cell's interlock bucket.

    One instance per robot process.  Cheap to construct; the bucket handle is
    resolved lazily on first use.

    Args:
        nats_client: a connected ``nats.NATS`` — typically ``ctx.nova.nats``.
        cell: cell id, e.g. ``"urw1-agr3-sk1"``.
        robot: this robot's id, e.g. ``"ir340r01"``.  Used as the holder identity.
        create_bucket: create the bucket if missing.  Safe for every process to
            set (creation is idempotent), but one owner is tidier.
    """

    def __init__(
        self, nats_client: nats.NATS, *, cell: str, robot: str, create_bucket: bool = True
    ):
        self._nats = nats_client
        self._cell = cell
        self._robot = robot
        self._run_id = uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]
        self._bucket_name = BUCKET_TEMPLATE.format(cell=cell)
        self._create_bucket = create_bucket
        self._kv: KeyValue | None = None
        self._kv_lock = asyncio.Lock()
        self._held: dict[str, int] = {}

    @property
    def robot(self) -> str:
        return self._robot

    @property
    def run_id(self) -> str:
        return self._run_id

    @property
    def held(self) -> list[str]:
        """Keys currently held by this client, for diagnostics."""
        return sorted(self._held)

    async def _bucket(self) -> KeyValue:
        async with self._kv_lock:
            if self._kv is not None:
                return self._kv
            if not self._nats.is_connected:
                raise RuntimeError(f"NATS client is not connected for: {self._nats.connected_url}")
            js = self._nats.jetstream()
            try:
                self._kv = await js.key_value(self._bucket_name)
            except NotFoundError:
                if not self._create_bucket:
                    raise RuntimeError(
                        f"Interlock bucket {self._bucket_name} missing and create_bucket=False"
                    ) from None
                logger.info("Creating interlock bucket %s", self._bucket_name)
                try:
                    self._kv = await js.create_key_value(
                        KeyValueConfig(
                            bucket=self._bucket_name,
                            max_value_size=_MAX_VALUE_SIZE,
                            max_bytes=_MAX_BUCKET_BYTES,
                            history=1,
                        )
                    )
                except BadRequestError:
                    # Lost the creation race to a sibling robot process — the
                    # whole cell starts its processes at once, so this is routine.
                    self._kv = await js.key_value(self._bucket_name)
            return self._kv

    async def _read(self, kv: KeyValue, key: str) -> tuple[LockRecord | None, int]:
        """Return the current record and revision, or ``(None, 0)`` if free.

        An unparseable payload is returned as a record held by
        :data:`CORRUPT_HOLDER`: it blocks acquisition like any foreign lock and
        stays visible to :meth:`inspect`, so the one tool an operator uses to
        find a lock that needs :meth:`force_release` can actually see it.
        """
        try:
            entry = await kv.get(key)
        except KeyNotFoundError:
            return None, 0
        if entry.value is None:
            return None, entry.revision or 0
        try:
            return LockRecord.model_validate_json(entry.value), entry.revision or 0
        except ValidationError:
            logger.warning("Corrupt interlock record at %s; treating as held", key)
            corrupt = LockRecord(
                holder=CORRUPT_HOLDER,
                run_id="",
                slot=0,
                label="unparseable record; force_release after confirming the zone is clear",
            )
            return corrupt, entry.revision or 0

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ acquire

    async def acquire(
        self,
        locks: Sequence[LockId],
        *,
        timeout: float = 120.0,
        label: str = "",
        poll_interval: float = 0.1,
    ) -> Grant:
        """Acquire every lock in *locks*, or none.  Blocks until granted.

        This is the ``MAKRO 20`` equivalent: pass the complete set of slots the
        step needs, exactly as the KRL sets ``A89``/``A91`` and then calls
        ``SPSMAKRO20`` once.

        Call it with the robot stationary, before planning or executing motion.

        Acquiring while already holding locks is refused (:class:`AlreadyHeldError`):
        the no-deadlock argument of this prototype is *no hold-and-wait*, so each
        step must take its complete slot set in one call.

        Raises:
            InterlockTimeout: nothing was acquired and the robot has not moved.
                Abort the program; never proceed.
            AlreadyHeldError: this client still holds locks from a previous
                acquire.  Release them first.
        """
        if not locks:
            return Grant(holder=self._robot, run_id=self._run_id, revisions={})
        if self._held:
            raise AlreadyHeldError(
                self._robot, sorted(self._held), sorted({lock.key for lock in locks})
            )

        kv = await self._bucket()
        by_key = {lock.key: lock for lock in locks}
        ordered = sorted(by_key)
        deadline = asyncio.get_running_loop().time() + timeout
        attempt = 0

        while True:
            taken: dict[str, int] = {}
            blocked_key: str | None = None

            for key in ordered:
                record = LockRecord(
                    holder=self._robot, run_id=self._run_id, slot=by_key[key].slot, label=label
                )
                payload = record.model_dump_json().encode()
                try:
                    taken[key] = await kv.create(key, payload)
                except (KeyWrongLastSequenceError, Exception) as exc:  # noqa: B014
                    if (
                        isinstance(exc, KeyWrongLastSequenceError)
                        or "wrong last sequence" in str(exc).lower()
                    ):
                        existing, revision = await self._read(kv, key)
                        if (
                            existing is not None
                            and existing.holder == self._robot
                            and existing.run_id == self._run_id
                        ):
                            # Our own lock from a previous partial attempt — adopt it.
                            taken[key] = revision
                            continue
                        blocked_key = key
                        break
                    raise

            if blocked_key is None:
                self._held.update(taken)
                logger.info(
                    "[%s] interlock acquired %s%s",
                    self._robot,
                    ordered,
                    f" ({label})" if label else "",
                )
                return Grant(holder=self._robot, run_id=self._run_id, revisions=taken)

            # Roll back completely.  Safe: the robot has not moved.
            await self._rollback(kv, taken)

            if asyncio.get_running_loop().time() >= deadline:
                blocked: dict[str, LockRecord | None] = {}
                for key in ordered:
                    record, _ = await self._read(kv, key)
                    if record is not None and record.holder != self._robot:
                        blocked[key] = record
                raise InterlockTimeout(self._robot, blocked, timeout)

            attempt += 1
            if attempt == 1 or attempt % 50 == 0:
                record, _ = await self._read(kv, blocked_key)
                logger.info(
                    "[%s] waiting for %s (held by %s)",
                    self._robot,
                    blocked_key,
                    record.holder if record else "<unknown>",
                )
            remaining = deadline - asyncio.get_running_loop().time()
            await self._wait_for_change(
                kv,
                blocked_key,
                max_wait=min(remaining, _WATCH_WAIT_CAP),
                poll_interval=poll_interval,
            )
            # Jitter breaks livelock between two robots contending for the same set.
            await asyncio.sleep(random.random() * poll_interval)

    async def _wait_for_change(
        self, kv: KeyValue, key: str, *, max_wait: float, poll_interval: float
    ) -> None:
        """Block until *key* changes, best-effort, at most *max_wait* seconds.

        Uses a KV watch when the bucket supports it, so a release wakes waiters
        immediately instead of on the next poll tick — contended hand-overs are
        on the cycle-time critical path.  Correctness never depends on the
        wake-up: on any watch failure this degrades to a jittered sleep, and the
        caller re-attempts the full acquire either way.
        """
        if max_wait <= 0:
            return
        fallback = min(poll_interval * (1.0 + random.random()), max_wait)
        watch = getattr(kv, "watch", None)
        if watch is None:
            await asyncio.sleep(fallback)
            return
        try:
            watcher = await watch(key)
        except Exception:
            await asyncio.sleep(fallback)
            return
        try:
            loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
            deadline = loop.time() + max_wait
            while True:
                remaining = deadline - loop.time()
                if remaining <= 0:
                    return
                try:
                    entry = await watcher.updates(timeout=remaining)
                except Exception:
                    return  # timed out — re-attempt from the acquire loop
                if entry is None:
                    # End of the initial replay.  The key may have been freed
                    # before the watch started — re-check instead of waiting
                    # for an update that will never come.
                    record, _ = await self._read(kv, key)
                    if record is None:
                        return
                    continue
                if getattr(entry, "operation", None) in (KV_DEL, KV_PURGE):
                    return
        finally:
            with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
                await watcher.stop()

    async def _rollback(self, kv: KeyValue, taken: dict[str, int]) -> None:
        # Guarded on the revision we created: if the entry changed hands in the
        # meantime (operator force_release + partner acquire) it is not ours to
        # delete, and the guard makes the delete a no-op instead of a clobber.
        for key, revision in taken.items():
            with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
                await kv.delete(key, last=revision)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ release

    async def release(self, grant: Grant, *, slots: Iterable[int] | None = None) -> None:
        """Release locks held under *grant*.

        This is the ``Freigabe Verriegelung`` equivalent — the KRL's
        ``A41/A49/A51 = EIN`` after the robot has retreated clear of the zone.
        **Call it only once the robot is physically out**, and as an awaited call,
        never as an ``io_write`` embedded in an action list.

        Args:
            slots: release only these of the holder's own slot numbers.  Omit to
                release everything in the grant.  Mirrors the KRL releasing a
                subset early (e.g. ``ir360r01`` drops slot 7 before the rest).
                Note that a partial release keeps the client "holding", so a
                further :meth:`acquire` is still refused until the rest is
                released too.  Slots already released under this grant are
                skipped by later calls, even if a partner has taken them since.

        Raises:
            ForeignRelease: some lock in the grant is now held by someone else,
                or — for a grant that was already fully released — by a newer
                grant of this same client.
                Everything that was still legitimately ours has been released;
                the foreign locks were left untouched.  Treat as a program
                abort — this robot's view of the cell has diverged.
        """
        kv = await self._bucket()
        wanted = set(slots) if slots is not None else None
        foreign: dict[str, LockRecord] = {}

        # A grant is live while any of its keys is still held at the revision it
        # took.  Keys of a live grant that are no longer held were released
        # earlier under it (a partial release) — a partner may legitimately hold
        # them by now, so they are skipped.  A spent grant is re-examined in
        # full: releasing it again is a stale handle, loud if anyone took over.
        live = any(self._held.get(key) == rev for key, rev in grant.revisions.items())

        for key, rev in sorted(grant.revisions.items()):
            if live and self._held.get(key) != rev:
                continue
            record, current_rev = await self._read(kv, key)
            if record is None:
                self._held.pop(key, None)
                continue
            if (
                record.holder != grant.holder
                or record.run_id != grant.run_id
                or current_rev != rev  # fencing: our own newer lock is not this grant's
            ):
                logger.error(
                    "[%s] refusing to release %s: held by %s/%s",
                    self._robot,
                    key,
                    record.holder,
                    record.run_id,
                )
                foreign[key] = record
                continue
            if wanted is not None and record.slot not in wanted:
                continue
            try:
                await kv.delete(key, last=current_rev)
            except KeyWrongLastSequenceError:
                # Changed hands between read and delete — re-classify.
                current, _ = await self._read(kv, key)
                if current is not None:
                    foreign[key] = current
                    continue
            self._held.pop(key, None)
            logger.info("[%s] interlock released %s", self._robot, key)

        if foreign:
            raise ForeignRelease(grant.holder, foreign)

    async def release_all(self, *, include_previous_runs: bool = False) -> list[str]:
        """Release everything this robot holds.  Returns the released keys.

        Mirrors the start-of-Folge ``A41..A56 = EIN`` block.  **Call it only when
        the robot is physically clear of every zone** — at home is the canonical
        case; in the incumbent the start-of-Folge release happens exactly there.
        Do *not* call it blindly from a ``finally:`` after an aborted motion: the
        robot may have stopped inside a zone, and releasing then is the collision
        scenario the no-TTL rule exists to prevent.  On abnormal exits, leave the
        locks held (see :meth:`hold`) and release from a known-clear position.

        Args:
            include_previous_runs: also release locks left behind by an earlier
                run of this robot's process (a crashed or restarted holder gets
                a fresh ``run_id``, so by default its locks are untouchable).
                This is the programmatic recovery for the routine restart case:
                by calling it the program asserts the robot is physically clear.
                Cross-robot cleanup remains an operator :meth:`force_release`.
        """
        kv = await self._bucket()
        keys = set(self._held)
        if include_previous_runs:
            with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
                keys.update(await kv.keys())

        released: list[str] = []
        for key in sorted(keys):
            record, revision = await self._read(kv, key)
            if record is None:
                self._held.pop(key, None)
                continue
            if record.holder != self._robot:
                continue
            if not include_previous_runs and record.run_id != self._run_id:
                continue
            with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
                await kv.delete(key, last=revision)
            self._held.pop(key, None)
            released.append(key)
            logger.info("[%s] interlock released %s (release_all)", self._robot, key)
        return released

    # ------------------------------------------------------------- context mgr

    @contextlib.asynccontextmanager
    async def hold(
        self, locks: Sequence[LockId], *, timeout: float = 120.0, label: str = ""
    ) -> AsyncIterator[Grant]:
        """``async with`` wrapper around :meth:`acquire` / :meth:`release`.

        Releases **only on a clean exit** of the block.  On an exception or a
        cancellation the locks are kept: a cancelled trajectory decelerates the
        robot over roughly a second and it may come to rest *inside* the shared
        zone, so releasing on the error path is exactly the "release a zone the
        robot is still in" hazard this design forbids.  The lock outliving a
        failed program is the safe direction — the partner waits.

        Recovery after an abnormal exit: move/confirm the robot clear (e.g. at
        home), then :meth:`release_all` — or ``release_all(include_previous_runs=True)``
        from the restarted process — or an operator :meth:`force_release`.
        """
        grant = await self.acquire(locks, timeout=timeout, label=label)
        try:
            yield grant
        except BaseException:
            logger.warning(
                "[%s] abnormal exit of interlocked block %s — keeping %s held; "
                "release_all() once the robot is confirmed clear",
                self._robot,
                f"({label})" if label else "",
                grant.keys,
            )
            raise
        else:
            await self.release(grant)

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- admin

    async def inspect(self) -> dict[str, LockRecord]:
        """Every currently-held lock in the cell.  For diagnostics and tooling."""
        kv = await self._bucket()
        out: dict[str, LockRecord] = {}
        try:
            keys = await kv.keys()
        except Exception:
            return out
        for key in keys:
            record, _ = await self._read(kv, key)
            if record is not None:
                out[key] = record
        return out

    async def force_release(self, key: str, *, reason: str) -> bool:
        """Clear a lock regardless of holder.

        Only for stale locks left by a crashed process, **after a human has
        confirmed the robot is physically clear of the zone**.  Loudly logged.

        Returns ``False`` if the key was already free, or if the lock changed
        hands between inspection and delete — in that case the operator's
        confirmation no longer describes the current holder, so nothing is
        touched; inspect again.
        """
        kv = await self._bucket()
        record, revision = await self._read(kv, key)
        if record is None and revision == 0:
            return False
        logger.warning(
            "[%s] FORCE RELEASE %s (was: %s) reason=%s",
            self._robot,
            key,
            record.holder if record else "<free>",
            reason,
        )
        try:
            await kv.delete(key, last=revision)
        except (KeyNotFoundError, KeyWrongLastSequenceError):
            logger.warning("[%s] force release of %s aborted: lock changed hands", self._robot, key)
            return False
        self._held.pop(key, None)
        return True


__all__ = [
    "CORRUPT_HOLDER",
    "AlreadyHeldError",
    "ForeignRelease",
    "Grant",
    "InterlockClient",
    "InterlockTimeout",
    "LockId",
    "LockRecord",
]

"""Data models for the robot↔robot interlock prototype.

Lock identity mirrors the VASS signal scheme it replaces.  In the source system a
shared zone between two robots is a *slot number* that both partners use
symmetrically: robot A requests slot N with ``A(80+N)`` and releases it with
``A(40+N)``; robot B does the same with the same N.  ``LockId`` reconstructs a
single canonical name from that pair, so both sides independently compute the
same string without any central registry.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import datetime
import re

import pydantic

_SAFE = re.compile(r"[^a-zA-Z0-9_=.-]")

#: NATS KV bucket, one per cell.  Mirrors ``nova_cells_{cell}_programs``.
BUCKET_TEMPLATE = "nova_cells_{cell}_interlocks"


def _clean(value: str) -> str:
    """NATS KV keys allow ``[-/_=.a-zA-Z0-9]``; we additionally exclude ``/`` and
    map anything unsafe to ``-``.  ``__`` separates the key components."""
    return _SAFE.sub("-", value)


class LockId(pydantic.BaseModel):
    """Canonical identity of one shared zone between exactly two robots.

    Built from the two robot ids and the VASS interlock slot number.  The slot
    number is symmetric in the source system — if ``ir340r01`` uses slot 9 for
    ``ir340r02`` then ``ir340r02`` uses slot 9 for ``ir340r01`` — which is what
    lets both processes derive the same key independently.  ``FB207`` enforces
    exactly this reciprocity (``xFehlerNr3``/``PAFE``); here the model validator
    normalises the pair to a canonical order and rejects self-interlocks, so a
    mismatched pair simply produces a key nobody else contends for.
    """

    model_config = pydantic.ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    robot_a: str
    robot_b: str
    slot: int = pydantic.Field(ge=1, le=16)

    @pydantic.model_validator(mode="after")
    def _order_and_check(self) -> "LockId":
        if self.robot_a == self.robot_b:
            raise ValueError(f"interlock slot {self.slot}: a robot cannot interlock with itself")
        if self.robot_a > self.robot_b:
            # Normalise to a canonical order so both partners derive the same key.
            # Bind both values first — assigning in place would alias.
            lo, hi = self.robot_b, self.robot_a
            object.__setattr__(self, "robot_a", lo)
            object.__setattr__(self, "robot_b", hi)
        return self

    @classmethod
    def of(cls, robot: str, partner: str, slot: int) -> "LockId":
        """Build from one robot's point of view. ``LockId.of("ir340r01", "ir340r02", 9)``."""
        return cls(robot_a=robot, robot_b=partner, slot=slot)

    @property
    def key(self) -> str:
        """The NATS KV key. Stable, and identical from either partner's side."""
        return f"{_clean(self.robot_a)}__{_clean(self.robot_b)}__v{self.slot}"

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        return self.key


class LockRecord(pydantic.BaseModel):
    """The value stored in the KV bucket while a lock is held."""

async def test_hold_keeps_locks_on_exception():
    """A failed Folge may have stopped the robot *inside* the zone — the lock
    must survive the error (fail-to-wait), never be released by control flow."""
    kv = FakeKV()
    r01 = make_client(kv, "ir340r01")
    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError):
        async with r01.hold([GEO40["r01_r02"]]):
            raise RuntimeError("folge failed")

    assert r01.held == [GEO40["r01_r02"].key], "abnormal exit must keep the lock"
    r02 = make_client(kv, "ir340r02")
    with pytest.raises(InterlockTimeout):

"""Data models for the robot↔robot interlock prototype.

Lock identity mirrors the VASS signal scheme it replaces.  In the source system a
shared zone between two robots is a *slot number* that both partners use
symmetrically: robot A requests slot N with ``A(80+N)`` and releases it with
``A(40+N)``; robot B does the same with the same N.  ``LockId`` reconstructs a
single canonical name from that pair, so both sides independently compute the
same string without any central registry.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import datetime
import re

import pydantic

_SAFE = re.compile(r"[^a-zA-Z0-9_=.-]")

#: NATS KV bucket, one per cell.  Mirrors ``nova_cells_{cell}_programs``.
BUCKET_TEMPLATE = "nova_cells_{cell}_interlocks"


def _clean(value: str) -> str:
    """NATS KV keys allow ``[-/_=.a-zA-Z0-9]``; we additionally exclude ``/`` and
    map anything unsafe to ``-``.  ``__`` separates the key components."""
    return _SAFE.sub("-", value)


class LockId(pydantic.BaseModel):
    """Canonical identity of one shared zone between exactly two robots.

    Built from the two robot ids and the VASS interlock slot number.  The slot
    number is symmetric in the source system — if ``ir340r01`` uses slot 9 for
    ``ir340r02`` then ``ir340r02`` uses slot 9 for ``ir340r01`` — which is what
    lets both processes derive the same key independently.  ``FB207`` enforces
    exactly this reciprocity (``xFehlerNr3``/``PAFE``); here the model validator
    normalises the pair to a canonical order and rejects self-interlocks, so a
    mismatched pair simply produces a key nobody else contends for.
    """

    model_config = pydantic.ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    robot_a: str
    robot_b: str
    slot: int = pydantic.Field(ge=1, le=16)

    @pydantic.model_validator(mode="after")
    def _order_and_check(self) -> "LockId":
        if self.robot_a == self.robot_b:
            raise ValueError(f"interlock slot {self.slot}: a robot cannot interlock with itself")
        if self.robot_a > self.robot_b:
            # Normalise to a canonical order so both partners derive the same key.
            # Bind both values first — assigning in place would alias.
            lo, hi = self.robot_b, self.robot_a
            object.__setattr__(self, "robot_a", lo)
            object.__setattr__(self, "robot_b", hi)
        return self

    @classmethod
    def of(cls, robot: str, partner: str, slot: int) -> "LockId":
        """Build from one robot's point of view. ``LockId.of("ir340r01", "ir340r02", 9)``."""
        return cls(robot_a=robot, robot_b=partner, slot=slot)

    @property
    def key(self) -> str:
        """The NATS KV key. Stable, and identical from either partner's side."""
        return f"{_clean(self.robot_a)}__{_clean(self.robot_b)}__v{self.slot}"

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        return self.key


class LockRecord(pydantic.BaseModel):
    """The value stored in the KV bucket while a lock is held."""

"""Tests for the NATS-backed robot↔robot interlock.

The unit tests run against an in-memory fake KV that reproduces the JetStream
semantics we rely on: ``create`` fails if the key exists, ``get`` raises
``KeyNotFoundError`` if it does not, ``delete(last=...)`` is revision-guarded,
and ``watch`` delivers DEL notifications.  ``test_interlock_live.py`` runs the
same protocol against a real broker (marked ``nats``; needs a local
``nats-server`` binary).
"""

import asyncio

import pytest
from nats.js.errors import KeyNotFoundError, KeyWrongLastSequenceError

from nova.interlock import (
    CORRUPT_HOLDER,
    AlreadyHeldError,
    ForeignRelease,
    Grant,
    InterlockClient,
    InterlockTimeout,
    LockId,
    LockRecord,
)

GEO40 = {
    "r01_r02": LockId.of("ir340r01", "ir340r02", 9),
    "r01_r03": LockId.of("ir340r01", "ir340r03", 11),
    "r02_r03": LockId.of("ir340r02", "ir340r03", 1),
}


# --------------------------------------------------------------------- fakes


class _Entry:
    def __init__(self, value: bytes | None, revision: int, operation: str | None = None):
        self.value = value
        self.revision = revision
        self.operation = operation


class _FakeWatcher:
    def __init__(self, initial: list[_Entry]):
        self._q: asyncio.Queue[_Entry | None] = asyncio.Queue()
        for entry in initial:
            self._q.put_nowait(entry)
        self._q.put_nowait(None)  # end-of-initial-replay marker, as nats-py sends

    def push(self, entry: _Entry) -> None:
        self._q.put_nowait(entry)

    async def updates(self, timeout: float = 5.0) -> _Entry | None:
        return await asyncio.wait_for(self._q.get(), timeout)

    async def stop(self) -> None:
        pass


class FakeKV:
    """Minimal JetStream KV stand-in with the atomicity guarantees we depend on."""

    def __init__(self):
        self._data: dict[str, _Entry] = {}
        self._rev = 0
        self.create_calls = 0
        self._watchers: dict[str, list[_FakeWatcher]] = {}

    def _notify(self, key: str, entry: _Entry) -> None:
        for watcher in self._watchers.get(key, []):
            watcher.push(entry)

    async def get(self, key: str) -> _Entry:
        if key not in self._data:
            raise KeyNotFoundError()
        return self._data[key]

    async def create(self, key: str, value: bytes, **_) -> int:
        self.create_calls += 1
        if key in self._data:
            raise KeyWrongLastSequenceError()
        self._rev += 1
        self._data[key] = _Entry(value, self._rev)
        self._notify(key, self._data[key])
        return self._rev

    async def delete(self, key: str, last: int | None = None, **_) -> bool:
        entry = self._data.get(key)
        if last is not None and (entry is None or entry.revision != last):
            raise KeyWrongLastSequenceError()
        if entry is None:
            return False
        del self._data[key]
        self._rev += 1
        self._notify(key, _Entry(None, self._rev, operation="DEL"))
        return True

    async def keys(self) -> list[str]:
        if not self._data:
            raise Exception("no keys")
        return list(self._data)

    async def watch(self, key: str, **_) -> _FakeWatcher:
        initial = [self._data[key]] if key in self._data else []
        watcher = _FakeWatcher(initial)
        self._watchers.setdefault(key, []).append(watcher)
        return watcher


def make_client(kv: FakeKV, robot: str) -> InterlockClient:
    client = InterlockClient.__new__(InterlockClient)
    client._nats = None  # ty: ignore[invalid-assignment]
    client._cell = "testcell"
    client._robot = robot
    client._run_id = f"run-{robot}"
    client._bucket_name = "nova_cells_testcell_interlocks"
    client._create_bucket = False
    client._kv = kv  # ty: ignore[invalid-assignment]
    client._kv_lock = asyncio.Lock()
    client._held = {}
    return client


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- lock identity


def test_lock_id_is_symmetric():
    """Both partners must derive the same key without coordinating."""
    for a, b, slot in [("ir340r01", "ir340r02", 9), ("ir340r01", "ir340r03", 11)]:
        assert LockId.of(a, b, slot).key == LockId.of(b, a, slot).key


def test_lock_id_distinguishes_slots():
    """Two robots can share several zones; each is its own lock."""
    assert LockId.of("ir360r01", "ir360r02", 1).key != LockId.of("ir360r01", "ir360r02", 2).key


def test_lock_id_rejects_self_interlock():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        LockId.of("ir340r01", "ir340r01", 9)


def test_lock_id_rejects_out_of_range_slot():
    for slot in (0, 17):
        with pytest.raises(ValueError):
            LockId.of("ir340r01", "ir340r02", slot)


def test_geo40_keys_are_distinct():
    assert len({lock.key for lock in GEO40.values()}) == 3


# -------------------------------------------------------------- acquire/release


async def test_acquire_and_release_roundtrip():
    kv = FakeKV()
    r01 = make_client(kv, "ir340r01")

    created so far in the bucket: nothing tracks them, so the partner would wait
    forever and release_all() could not find them."""
    kv = FakeKV()

    assert r01.held == []

    kv = FakeKV()

    assert record.holder == "ir340r02"

        r01.acquire([GEO40["r01_r02"]], timeout=0.3, poll_interval=0.01),
        return_exceptions=True,
    )
    grants = [r for r in results if isinstance(r, Grant)]
    refused = [r for r in results if isinstance(r, AlreadyHeldError)]
    assert len(grants) == 1 and len(refused) == 1, results

"""Data models for the robot↔robot interlock prototype.

Lock identity mirrors the VASS signal scheme it replaces.  In the source system a
shared zone between two robots is a *slot number* that both partners use
symmetrically: robot A requests slot N with ``A(80+N)`` and releases it with
``A(40+N)``; robot B does the same with the same N.  ``LockId`` reconstructs a
single canonical name from that pair, so both sides independently compute the
same string without any central registry.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import datetime
import re

import pydantic

_SAFE = re.compile(r"[^a-zA-Z0-9_=.-]")

#: NATS KV bucket, one per cell.  Mirrors ``nova_cells_{cell}_programs``.
BUCKET_TEMPLATE = "nova_cells_{cell}_interlocks"


def _clean(value: str) -> str:
    """NATS KV keys allow ``[-/_=.a-zA-Z0-9]``; we additionally exclude ``/`` and
    map anything unsafe to ``-``.  ``__`` separates the key components."""
    return _SAFE.sub("-", value)


class LockId(pydantic.BaseModel):
    """Canonical identity of one shared zone between exactly two robots.

    Built from the two robot ids and the VASS interlock slot number.  The slot
    number is symmetric in the source system — if ``ir340r01`` uses slot 9 for
    ``ir340r02`` then ``ir340r02`` uses slot 9 for ``ir340r01`` — which is what
    lets both processes derive the same key independently.  ``FB207`` enforces
    exactly this reciprocity (``xFehlerNr3``/``PAFE``); here the model validator
    normalises the pair to a canonical order and rejects self-interlocks, so a
    mismatched pair simply produces a key nobody else contends for.
    """

    model_config = pydantic.ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    robot_a: str
    robot_b: str
    slot: int = pydantic.Field(ge=1, le=16)

    @pydantic.model_validator(mode="after")
    def _order_and_check(self) -> "LockId":
        if self.robot_a == self.robot_b:
            raise ValueError(f"interlock slot {self.slot}: a robot cannot interlock with itself")
        if self.robot_a > self.robot_b:
            # Normalise to a canonical order so both partners derive the same key.
            # Bind both values first — assigning in place would alias.
            lo, hi = self.robot_b, self.robot_a
            object.__setattr__(self, "robot_a", lo)
            object.__setattr__(self, "robot_b", hi)
        return self

    @classmethod
    def of(cls, robot: str, partner: str, slot: int) -> "LockId":
        """Build from one robot's point of view. ``LockId.of("ir340r01", "ir340r02", 9)``."""
        return cls(robot_a=robot, robot_b=partner, slot=slot)

    @property
    def key(self) -> str:
        """The NATS KV key. Stable, and identical from either partner's side."""
        return f"{_clean(self.robot_a)}__{_clean(self.robot_b)}__v{self.slot}"

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        return self.key


class LockRecord(pydantic.BaseModel):
    """The value stored in the KV bucket while a lock is held."""

    holder: str
    """Robot id of the holder, e.g. ``ir340r01``."""

    run_id: str
    """Unique per process run.  Distinguishes a restarted process from its predecessor."""

    slot: int
    """The holder's own VASS slot number — kept for traceability back to ``A8x``/``A4x``."""

    label: str = ""
    """Free-text, e.g. the Folge step that took the lock. Diagnostics only."""

    acquired_at: datetime.datetime = pydantic.Field(
        default_factory=lambda: datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc)
    )

    def age_seconds(self) -> float:
        now = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc)
        return (now - self.acquired_at).total_seconds()


class Grant(pydantic.BaseModel):
    """Handle returned by a successful acquire.  Carries the fencing revisions."""

    model_config = pydantic.ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    holder: str
    run_id: str
    revisions: dict[str, int]
    """KV key -> revision at the moment we took it.  Release is conditional on these."""

    @property
    def keys(self) -> list[str]:
        return sorted(self.revisions)


class InterlockError(Exception):
    """Base class for interlock failures."""


class InterlockTimeout(InterlockError):
    """Acquire did not succeed within the timeout.

    The robot has **not** moved and holds nothing: acquisition is all-or-nothing and
    rolls back on failure.  Treat as a program abort, never as permission to proceed.
    """

    def __init__(self, holder: str, blocked_on: dict[str, LockRecord | None], timeout: float):
        self.holder = holder
        self.blocked_on = blocked_on
        self.timeout = timeout
        detail = ", ".join(
            f"{k} held by {v.holder if v else '<unknown>'}"
            + (f" for {v.age_seconds():.1f}s" if v else "")
            for k, v in blocked_on.items()
        )
        super().__init__(f"{holder} waited {timeout:.1f}s for: {detail or '<no detail>'}")


class AlreadyHeldError(InterlockError):
    """``acquire()`` was called while this client already holds locks.

    The deadlock argument of this prototype is *no hold-and-wait*: a robot never
    waits for locks while holding others, because each step takes its **complete**
    slot set in a single all-or-nothing :meth:`InterlockClient.acquire` — exactly
    like one ``SPSMAKRO20`` call.  Acquiring while holding would reintroduce
    hold-and-wait (and with it, representable deadlock), so it is refused.

    Release everything first, or widen the original acquire to the full set.
    """

    def __init__(self, robot: str, held: list[str], requested: list[str]):
        self.robot = robot
        self.held = held
        self.requested = requested
        super().__init__(
            f"{robot} tried to acquire {requested} while already holding {held}; "
            "all-or-nothing interlocking forbids hold-and-wait — release first, "
            "or take the complete set in one acquire()"
        )


class ForeignRelease(InterlockError):
    """A lock from this grant is now held by someone else (or a newer run).

    Raised by :meth:`InterlockClient.release` **after** releasing every lock in
    the grant that was still legitimately ours; the foreign locks listed here
    were left untouched.  This means the caller's view of what it holds has
    diverged from the cell (e.g. an operator ``force_release`` while this robot
    believed it held the zone) — treat it as a program abort and investigate.
    """

    def __init__(self, holder: str, records: dict[str, LockRecord]):
        self.holder = holder
        self.records = records
        detail = ", ".join(f"{k} held by {v.holder}/{v.run_id}" for k, v in records.items())
        super().__init__(f"{holder} attempted to release locks it no longer holds: {detail}")

async def test_roundtrip_against_jetstream(nc, cell):
    r01 = InterlockClient(nc, cell=cell, robot="ir340r01")
    lock = LockId.of("ir340r01", "ir340r02", 9)

    grant = await r01.acquire([lock], label="live roundtrip")
    assert r01.held == [lock.key]
    state = await r01.inspect()
    assert state[lock.key].holder == "ir340r01"

    await r01.release(grant)
    assert await r01.inspect() == {}


async def test_mutual_exclusion_and_watch_wakeup(nc, cell):
    r01 = InterlockClient(nc, cell=cell, robot="ir340r01")
    r02 = InterlockClient(nc, cell=cell, robot="ir340r02")
    lock = LockId.of("ir340r01", "ir340r02", 9)

    grant = await r01.acquire([lock])
    waiter = asyncio.create_task(r02.acquire([lock], timeout=10, poll_interval=0.05))
    await asyncio.sleep(0.3)
    assert not waiter.done(), "r02 must not enter while r01 holds the zone"

    released_at = asyncio.get_running_loop().time()
    await r01.release(grant)
    second = await asyncio.wait_for(waiter, timeout=5)
    handover = asyncio.get_running_loop().time() - released_at
    assert second.holder == "ir340r02"
    assert handover < 2.0, f"hand-over took {handover:.2f}s — watch wake-up seems dead"
